name: Igal
overview: Igal is a male figure from the tribe of Judah, identified specifically as the son of Shecaniah. Beyond his lineage, Scripture does not provide additional details or notable events concerning him. His mention is concise, reflecting a genealogical record within the tribe of Judah.
namesAndTitles: The name Igal is a proper name meaning 'he redeems.' This meaning offers insight into the character of the name but is not indicated as being given directly by God. The name appears in the genealogical context of 1 Chronicles 3:22.
familyAndRelationships: Igal is explicitly recorded as the son of Shemaiah, establishing a clear father-son relationship. No other family relationships are documented in Scripture beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Igal's significance lies primarily in his inclusion within the genealogical records of Judah, emphasizing the continuity of the tribe through generations. His mention as the son of Shecaniah situates him within the post-exilic community, underscoring the preservation of lineage and heritage important to God's covenant people.
